# Harbor & Pine starter site

The practice website for the Data Privacy cohort. You deploy your own copy to **GitHub Pages** (free, public, HTTPS), and every Securiti lab in Sessions 1–3 runs against it.

> **Fictional site.** Never enter real personal data. Use plus-addressed test emails only (`you+anything@veeam.com`).<!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c1 -->

<!-- gdoc_comment_end: c1 -->

---

## What's in here

| File | Purpose | Used in |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `index.html`, `about.html`, `contact.html`, `privacy.html` | Four pages so the scanner has something to crawl | S1–S3 |
| `assets/js/analytics.js` | Stand-in analytics tag. Sets `hp_analytics_id`, `hp_last_page` and localStorage `hp_session_start` | S1–S2 |
| `assets/js/marketing-pixel.js` | Stand-in ad pixel. Sets `hp_ad_click` | S1–S2 |
| <!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c2 -->Inline<!-- gdoc_comment_end: c2 --> script at the bottom of `index.html` | A/B test bucket. Sets `hp_ab_variant` | S2 fault |
| `assets/js/chat-widget.js` | Sets `hp_chat_session` **only after a click** | S1 fault |
| YouTube iframe on `index.html` | Third-party cookies | S2 discussion |
| `contact.html` newsletter form | Becomes a Form-Based Consent endpoint | S3 |
| `privacy.html` iframe placeholder | Where the published privacy notice goes | S2 |
| `SECURITI-*` comment markers | Where you paste Securiti code | S2–S3 |
| `sitemap.xml` | Optional, for Sitemap Scanning | S1 |

**Some of this site is broken on purpose.** Don't "fix" anything before the lab tells you to. The break-fix exercises depend on it.

---

## Deploy to GitHub Pages (about 10 minutes)

### Use a *user site*, not a project site&nbsp;

Create a repository named **exactly** `<your-github-username>.github.io`. That publishes the site at the root of `https://<username>.github.io/`.<!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c3 -->

<!-- gdoc_comment_end: c3 -->Don't use a project site (`https://<username>.github.io/<repo>/`). Securiti's docs don't say whether the cookie scanner handles a site that lives under a subpath, so we avoid the question entirely.

### Steps

Sign in to GitHub. Create a free account with your personal email if you don't have one.

**New repository** → name: `<username>.github.io` → **Public** → **Create repository**.

**Add file → Upload files** → drag in the *contents* of this `starter-site` folder, including the `assets` folder and the hidden `.nojekyll` file → **Commit changes**.

- Open the folder first and select its contents. Don't drag the `starter-site` folder itself, or the site publishes at `/starter-site/` and the root returns 404\.  
  - On macOS, press `Cmd + Shift + .` (period) in Finder to show hidden files so you can see `.nojekyll` (empty, 0 bytes). Don't upload `.DS_Store`.  
  - Can't find `.nojekyll`? In the repo: **Add file → Create new file** → name `.nojekyll`, leave it blank → **Commit changes**. The site works without it; it just skips Jekyll processing.

**<!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c4 -->Settings → Pages** → Source: **Deploy from a branch** → Branch: `main` / `(root)` → **Save**.<!-- gdoc_comment_end: c4 -->![][image1]

Wait 1–3 minutes, then open `https://<username>.github.io/`. You should see the Harbor & Pine homepage.  <!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c5 -->Example: <!-- gdoc_comment_end: c5 -->![][image2]

<!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c6 -->In Chrome, open DevTools → **Application → Cookies** → your site. You should see `hp_analytics_id`, `hp_last_page`, `hp_ab_variant` and `hp_ad_click`.<!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c7 --> If you do, the site is working.<!-- gdoc_comment_end: c7 --><!-- gdoc_comment_end: c6 -->![][image3]

![][image4]<!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c8 -->

<!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c9 --><!-- gdoc_comment_end: c8 -->**What do we do if we do not see the cookies?<!-- gdoc_comment_end: c9 -->**

![][image5]

### Editing later

For the labs you'll edit HTML directly in GitHub: open the file → pencil icon → edit → **Commit changes**.

**Every commit takes 1–10 minutes to go live, and browsers cache the old version.** After a commit:

1. Open the repository's **Actions** tab and wait for the "pages build and deployment" run to finish (green check).  
2. Hard-reload the page (`Cmd+Shift+R`), or test in an Incognito window.

Most "my change didn't work" problems in this cohort are this delay.

---

## Why GitHub Pages and not your laptop?

Securiti's cookie scanner runs in Securiti's cloud, so the site must be reachable from the public internet. The docs say the domain must be "valid and reachable". There's no private-network scan path for Cookie Consent. A site on `localhost` can't be scanned. Exposing your laptop through a tunnelling tool is fragile: the tunnel dies when the laptop sleeps, endpoint security often flags it, and some free tunnels put a warning page in front of the site, which the scanner then scans instead. GitHub Pages gives you a stable public HTTPS URL with nothing in front of it.

---

## Don't enable "Use top-level domain to track consent status"

`github.io` is on the Public Suffix List, so browsers won't let any site set cookies on `github.io` itself. Your consent cookies stay on `<username>.github.io`, which is the behavior you want. Leave that banner toggle **off**.

    head:
      author: Bill Klaver
      time: '2026-10-26T20:03:58.250Z'
      body: 'Include a screen shot of what to look for see my example. Claude helped
        me navigate with the following:<br>1. Settings: the tab at the top of your
        repository page (the row with Code, Issues, Pull requests, Actions, and so
        on). It’s usually the far right tab, sometimes tucked under a “...” menu on
        smaller screens.<br>2. Pages: in the left sidebar of the Settings screen,
        scroll down to the “Code and automation” section and click Pages.<br>3. Source:
        Deploy from a branch: a dropdown near the top of the Pages screen (it may
        sit under “Build and deployment”). It asks how GitHub should publish your
        site. Choose Deploy from a branch, which means “publish whatever files are
        in one of my repo’s branches.” The other option, GitHub Actions, is for more
        advanced build setups.<br>4. Branch: main / (root): after choosing the source,
        two more dropdowns appear.<br>The first is the branch. A branch is a version
        of your repo’s files, and main is the default one. Select main.<br>The second
        is the folder. Select / (root), which means the top level of the repo, where
        your index.html lives. The other choice, /docs, would only be used if your
        site files were in a folder named docs.<br>5. Save: click the Save button
        next to those dropdowns.'
      quote: 'Settings → Pages → Source: Deploy from a branch → Branch: main / (root)
        → Save.'
